name: Chana Ghugni
ingredients: 2 cups dried black chickpeas (kala chana), soaked overnight
instructions: 1. Pressure cook the soaked black chickpeas with water and a pinch of salt until soft and tender.
2. Heat mustard oil in a heavy-bottomed pan until it smokes slightly, then add cumin seeds and bay leaves.
3. Add chopped onions and sauté until golden brown.
4. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and cook for a minute, then add tomatoes, turmeric, coriander, and chili powder.
5. Cook the masala until the oil separates from the sides.
6. Add the boiled chickpeas with their cooking water to the pan.
7. Simmer on low heat for 10-15 minutes until the gravy thickens.
8. Finish with garam masala and garnish generously with fresh coriander.
description: Chana Ghugni is a quintessential Bihari street food, cherished as a hearty breakfast or an evening snack. It is often served with flattened rice (chura) or puffed rice (muri) and holds deep cultural roots as a quick, nutritious, and soul-satisfying comfort food found across Bihar's household kitchens and local food stalls.
